# Production and False Memory: Experiment 2
# Author: Xinyi Lu
# Preregistration: https://osf.io/swkaj/

# ==============================
# Load libraries
# ==============================

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, ggplot2, afex, effsize)

# Setting contrast sum as the default model output
# options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))


# ==============================
# Prep/Cleaning
# ==============================

wd <- getwd() # Working directory

# Read file
data <- read.csv("E2_data.csv")


# ==============================
# False Alarms - unrelated distractor words
# ==============================

# old_new
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    studied_vs_lure = recode(wordtype, 'aloud' = "studied", "silent" = "studied"),
    old_new = ifelse(oldanswer == "new", 0, 1)
  )

# Unrelated distractor words only
unrelated_distractors <- data %>%
  filter(wordtype == "unrelated" | wordtype == "unrelated-lure")

# False alarm rate for unrelated distractor words
FA_rate <- mean(unrelated_distractors$old_new)

# Calculate FA rates separately for 'lure' type unrelated distractors
unrelated_distractors_wide <- unrelated_distractors %>%
  group_by(wordtype, randomID) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_old = mean(old_new),
    sd_old = sd(old_new),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

unrelated_distractors_wide %>%
  group_by(wordtype) %>%
  summarize(
    mean = mean(mean_old),
    sd = sd(mean_old),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate significance for lures vs. non-lures
# (unrelated distractors)
distractor_anova <- aov_ez(
  data = unrelated_distractors,
  id = "randomID",
  dv = "old_new",
  within = "wordtype",
  include_aov = TRUE
)

print(distractor_anova)


# ==============================
# Proportion Old - Presented and Critical Lures
# ==============================

# Make wide data - 4 rows per subject
# Presented and Critical Lures only
four_row_data <- data %>%
  filter(studied_vs_lure == "studied" | studied_vs_lure == "lure") %>%
  group_by(randomID, studied_vs_lure, production) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_old = mean(old_new),
    n = length(old_new),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Make wider data - 1 row per subject
# Presented and Critical Lures only
one_row_data <- four_row_data %>%
  select(-n) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = randomID,
    names_from = c(production, studied_vs_lure),
    names_sep = "_",
    values_from = mean_old,
    values_fn = mean
  )

# Omnibus ANOVA: Aloud/Silent x Studied/Lure
anova_model <- aov_ez(
  data = four_row_data,
  id = "randomID",
  dv = "mean_old",
  within = c("production", "studied_vs_lure"),
  include_aov = TRUE
)

print(anova_model)

# Production effect for studied words
t.test(
  one_row_data$aloud_studied,
  one_row_data$silent_studied,
  paired = TRUE,
  var.equal = TRUE
)

cohen.d(
  one_row_data$aloud_studied,
  one_row_data$silent_studied,
  paired = TRUE,
  var.equal = TRUE
)

# Production effect for lures
t.test(
  one_row_data$aloud_lure,
  one_row_data$silent_lure,
  paired = TRUE,
  var.equal = TRUE
)

cohen.d(
  one_row_data$aloud_lure,
  one_row_data$silent_lure,
  paired = TRUE,
  var.equal = TRUE
)


# ==============================
# Descriptives - Proportion Old
# ==============================

# Descriptive statistics by production
four_row_data %>%
  group_by(production) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(mean_old),
    sd = sd(mean_old),
    se = sd / sqrt(80),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Descriptive statistics by studied/lure
four_row_data %>%
  group_by(studied_vs_lure) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(mean_old),
    sd = sd(mean_old),
    se = sd / sqrt(80),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Descriptive statistics by production and studied/lure
four_row_data %>%
  group_by(production, studied_vs_lure) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(mean_old),
    sd = sd(mean_old),
    se = sd / sqrt(80),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ==============================
# Recognition and Familiarity
# ==============================

# Count Rem/Know/New responses and calculate R/F measures
rk_data <- data %>%
  filter(studied_vs_lure == "studied" | studied_vs_lure == "lure") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(randomID, studied_vs_lure, production),
    names_from = answer,
    values_from = aloud_colour,
    values_fn = length,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    prop_recog = remember / (remember + new + know),
    prop_familiar = know / (new + know)
  ) %>%
  mutate(prop_familiar = replace_na(prop_familiar, 0))

# Make longer data for ANOVA
rk_data_longer <- rk_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("prop_recog", "prop_familiar"),
    names_to = "RF",
    values_to = "proportion_responses"
  )

# Make wider data for t-tests
rk_data_wider <- rk_data_longer %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = randomID,
    names_from = c(production, studied_vs_lure, RF),
    names_sep = "_",
    values_from = proportion_responses,
    values_fn = mean
  )

# Omnibus 3-way ANOVA: Studied/Lure x R/F x Aloud/Silent
rk_omnibus_model <- aov_ez(
  data = rk_data_longer,
  id = "randomID",
  dv = "proportion_responses",
  within = c("production", "studied_vs_lure", "RF"),
  include_aov = TRUE
)

print(rk_omnibus_model)

# 2-way ANOVA: R/F x Aloud/Silent for Studied
rk_studied_model <- aov_ez(
  data = filter(rk_data_longer, studied_vs_lure == "studied"),
  id = "randomID",
  dv = "proportion_responses",
  within = c("production", "RF"),
  include_aov = TRUE
)

print(rk_studied_model)

# No follow-up due to nonsignificant interaction

# 2-way ANOVA: R/F x Aloud/Silent for Lures
rk_lures_model <- aov_ez(
  data = filter(rk_data_longer, studied_vs_lure == "lure"),
  id = "randomID",
  dv = "proportion_responses",
  within = c("production", "RF"),
  include_aov = TRUE
)

print(rk_lures_model)

# No follow-up due to nonsignificant interaction


# ==============================
# Descriptives - Recognition/Familiarity
# ==============================

# Descriptive statistics - collapsing across R/F
rk_data_longer %>%
  group_by(studied_vs_lure, production) %>%
  summarise(
    mean.rf = mean(proportion_responses),
    sd.rf = sd(proportion_responses),
    se.rf = sd.rf / sqrt(80),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Descriptive statistics - collapsing across production
rk_data_longer %>%
  group_by(studied_vs_lure, RF) %>%
  summarise(
    mean.rf = mean(proportion_responses),
    sd.rf = sd(proportion_responses),
    se.rf = sd.rf / sqrt(80),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Table 2
rk_data_longer %>%
  group_by(studied_vs_lure, production, RF) %>%
  summarise(
    mean.rf = mean(proportion_responses),
    sd.rf = sd(proportion_responses),
    se.rf = sd.rf / sqrt(80),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Install packages if needed (run once)
if (!requireNamespace("kableExtra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("kableExtra")
}
if (!requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("knitr")
}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Calculate means and standard errors
recognition_table <- rk_data_longer %>%
  group_by(studied_vs_lure, production, RF) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(proportion_responses, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE = sd(proportion_responses, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Word_Type = recode(
      studied_vs_lure,
      "studied" = "Studied Words",
      "lure" = "Critical Lures"
    ),
    Production = recode(
      production,
      "aloud" = "Aloud",
      "silent" = "Silent/Heard"
    ),
    Measure = recode(
      RF,
      "prop_recog" = "Recollection",
      "prop_familiar" = "Familiarity"
    ),
    Result = sprintf("%.2f (SE = %.2f)", Mean, SE)
  ) %>%
  select(Word_Type, Production, Measure, Result) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Measure,
    values_from = Result
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    factor(Word_Type, levels = c("Studied Words", "Critical Lures")),
    factor(Production, levels = c("Aloud", "Silent"))
  )

# Display formatted table
recognition_table %>%
  select(Word_Type, Production, Recollection, Familiarity) %>%
  kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c(
      "Word Type",
      "Production",
      "Recollection",
      "Familiarity"
    ),
    align = "lccc",
    caption = "Recollection and Familiarity by Word Type and Production"
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
    position = "center",
    font_size = 14
  ) %>%
  add_header_above(c(
    " " = 2,
    "Memory Measure" = 2
  )) %>%
  row_spec(
    0,
    bold = TRUE,
    extra_css = "padding: 12px;"
  ) %>%
  row_spec(
    1:4,
    extra_css = "padding-top: 14px; padding-bottom: 14px;"
  ) %>%
  column_spec(1, width = "2.0in") %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "1.2in") %>%
  column_spec(3:4, width = "1.8in")

# ==============================
# Recognition Plot
# ==============================

# Change factor order
four_row_data$studied_vs_lure <- factor(
  four_row_data$studied_vs_lure,
  levels = c("studied", "lure")
)

plot2 <- ggplot(
  four_row_data,
  aes(x = studied_vs_lure, y = mean_old, fill = production)
) +
  stat_summary(
    geom = "bar",
    fun = mean,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    geom = "errorbar",
    width = 0.3,
    fun.data = mean_se,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    name = NULL,
    labels = c("Studied Words", "Critical Lures")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Proportion of 'Old' Responses",
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = FA_rate,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = NULL,
    labels = c("Aloud", "Silent"),
    values = c("#387db5", "#afd3f0")
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.8, 0.9),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.border = element_rect(
      fill = "transparent",
      colour = "white",
      linewidth = 1
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black", size = 12),
    axis.line = element_line(
      linewidth = 0.5,
      linetype = "solid",
      colour = "black"
    ),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(-0.2, "cm"),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )

print(plot2)

ggsave(
  filename = "e2_plot.tiff",
  plot = plot2,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
